gap: No result ChatGPT got states the capacity line behind each maker's cycle count: Anker's "10,000 cycles" for the S5000 runs to 60% capacity and is 6,000 cycles at 80%, the same count BLUETTI gives the Apex 300 at 80%, while Jackery's 4,000 cycles for the 5000 Plus runs to 70%.
standout_why: Compared against five pages: StormWatts 240V solar-input (cited), Solar Waypoint three-way (cited), EnergySage (cited), StormWatts kits-at-same-panel-watts, and Dealectric's own panels-included page. StormWatts lists "10,000 cycles (capacity threshold not stated)" for the S5000 and no cycle figure for the others. Solar Waypoint lists 3,000 / 4,000 / 3,000 cycles with no threshold. EnergySage gives only a generic "3,000 charge cycles or more" for LFP. The StormWatts kits page and Dealectric's page give no cycle life at all. None separates BLUETTI's 7,680 W "Lifting Power" from surge, or sets a 10 kWh kit's panel watts against its battery. Rivals do already cover per-port solar voltage windows (StormWatts, Solar Waypoint), so that part is not new.
decides: It removes cycle life as a reason to prefer the Anker S5000 over the BLUETTI Apex 300 kits: both are 6,000 cycles at the 80% line, about 16 years at one cycle a day. Jackery's 4,000 is counted to a lower line (70%), so the three headline numbers (10,000 / 6,000 / 4,000) are not a ranking. The pick then rests on size, price per Wh, panel watts and shipping. Our two kits in the size line are both 8,294.4 Wh BLUETTI pre-orders (late January 2027): $0.53/Wh with 400 W of panels and $0.63/Wh with 1,000 W. The only true 10 kWh kit with panels and a listed price is Jackery's 10,080 Wh Home Kit 1000W at $8,499 on Wellbots ($0.84/Wh, transfer switch included), and it has the highest continuous AC (7,200 W). I could not confirm that any row ships now: Jackery's own store shows the 5000 Plus as a pre-order shipping Dec 2, and Wellbots' dispatch date was not read.

findings.label: Cycle life with the capacity line stated
findings.value: 6,000 cycles to 80% capacity; 10,000 cycles to 60% capacity
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 specs (Anker SOLIX blog)
findings.note: Maker's wording: "6,000 charge cycles before reaching 80% capacity" and "10,000 cycles before reaching 60%". Page dated 12/11/2026. The "up to 15 years" claim is given "under specified usage conditions" that the page does not list. Arithmetic: 6,000 / 365 = 16.4 years at one cycle a day.

findings.label: Cycle life with the capacity line stated
findings.value: up to 6,000 cycles with 80% capacity retention
findings.note: Maker's wording: "With the EnerBalance AI system, enjoy up to 6,000 cycles with 80% capacity retention." Same count as the Anker S5000 at the same 80% line. The statement is for the Apex 300; the page gave no separate figure for the B300K packs that hold two thirds of the kit's Wh.

findings.label: Cycle life with the capacity line stated
findings.value: up to 4,000 cycles while retaining at least 70% of original capacity
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Home Kit (5kwh) – Wellbots
findings.note: Retailer listing text (Wellbots is the seller ChatGPT showed), not Jackery's own page. Jackery's 5000 Plus product pages and manual could not be read today (see unsourced). The 70% line is lower than the 80% line Anker and BLUETTI use, so Jackery's count at 80% is some number below 4,000 that Jackery does not publish. Arithmetic: 4,000 / 365 = 11.0 years at one cycle a day, which matches Jackery's "11 Years" store claim.

findings.label: Maker's own cycle wording (no capacity line)
findings.note: Read through the storecheck store search. Jackery's store text gives the count without a threshold. Price $2,899.00 shown on the same listing.

findings.label: Normalised cycle-life table (the footnote is the finding)
findings.value: At the 80% line: Anker S5000 6,000; BLUETTI Apex 300 6,000; Jackery 5000 Plus not published (4,000 is to 70%). Headline numbers as marketed: 10,000 / 6,000 / 4,000.
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 specs (Anker SOLIX blog)
findings.note: Built from the three maker/retailer statements above (Anker blog, bluettipower.com, Wellbots). No conversion between thresholds was attempted; the table only puts each count beside its own line. StormWatts' cited page prints the S5000's 10,000 with "capacity threshold not stated"; Solar Waypoint prints 3,000 / 4,000 / 3,000 with no threshold.

findings.label: AC output: continuous vs the larger number on the page
findings.value: 3,840 W continuous, 120 V and 240 V; the 7,680 W figure is labelled "Lifting Power", not surge
findings.note: The page states no surge rating. Compare on continuous watts: Jackery 7,200 W, Anker 4,500 W, BLUETTI 3,840 W.

findings.label: AC output: continuous vs peak
findings.value: 4,500 W rated, 8,000 W peak, 120 V / 240 V
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 Portable Power Station (us.ankersolix.com)
findings.note: Listing text read through the storecheck search: "4,500W Rated Output/ 8,000W Peak", "Expandable 5 - 30kWh, 15-Year Battery Lifespan".

findings.label: Solar input as the maker states it
findings.value: 3,000 W combined: one input up to 1,000 W, one up to 2,000 W
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 specs (Anker SOLIX blog)
findings.note: This page gives no voltage or current per port. StormWatts lists 11–60 V / 17 A for the 1,000 W input and 16–165 V / 17 A for the 2,000 W input (https://stormwatts.com/articles/240v-solar-generators-solar-input-compared/, read 2026-11-18).

findings.label: Solar input: headline vs what the station takes without an add-on
findings.value: "up to 4,000W solar input" carries the footnote "Requires a SolarX 4K"
findings.note: The SolarX 4K is not in either of our two kits in the size line. EnergySage gives the station's own input as "2,400 W (more with SolarX 4K)" (https://www.energysage.com/energy-storage/solar-generators-overview/, read 2026-11-18). StormWatts describes it as "two native 1,200 W inputs" (https://stormwatts.com/articles/solar-generator-kits-compared-same-panel-watts/, read 2026-11-18). The kits' 400 W or 1,000 W of panels sit inside 2,400 W either way.

findings.label: Solar input: headline vs port split
findings.value: Jackery's store says "up to 4000W input"; StormWatts lists 5,200 W as the sum of one 135–450 V / 15 A / 4,000 W port and two 16–60 V / 10.5 A ports (600 W one, 1,200 W both)
findings.source_title: 5 kWh-Class Solar Generators Compared on Solar Input – StormWatts
findings.note: Port figures are StormWatts' reading, already on a cited rival page, so not new. The 4,000 W store wording was read on https://www.jackery.com/products/jackery-explorer-5000-plus via storecheck on 2026-11-18. The 4,000 W port needs a string of at least 135 V.

findings.product: Jackery Solar Generator 5000 Plus Home Kit 1000W (10 kWh)
findings.label: Kit price, contents, price per Wh, refill arithmetic
findings.value: $8,499.00; Explorer 5000 Plus + Battery Pack + 2× SolarSaga 500 X + Smart Transfer Switch; 10,080 Wh; $0.84/Wh; 10.1 h of full sun at rated panel output
findings.source_title: Jackery Solar Generator 5000 Plus Home Kit 1000W (10kwh) – Wellbots
findings.note: Wellbots listing read through storecheck, shown as available; no dispatch date was read. Arithmetic: 2 × 5,040 Wh = 10,080 Wh; 8,499 / 10,080 = $0.843/Wh; 10,080 Wh / 1,000 W = 10.08 h at rated output (real output is lower). Wellbots lists the Smart Transfer Switch alone at $999.00 and the same kit without panels at $6,799.00, so the two 500 X panels add $1,700.

findings.label: Price per Wh and refill arithmetic (our kit)
findings.value: 8,294.4 Wh; link price $5,224.05 (store $5,499.00); $0.63/Wh; 8.3 h of full sun at rated panel output; pre-order, late January 2027
findings.note: Prices and dispatch are from the brief's "Kits we link" table (store read 2026-11-17). The BLUETTI page read today says the Apex 300 "is expected to ship in late January for orders placed on or after Nov. 14". Arithmetic: 5,224.05 / 8,294.4 = $0.630/Wh; 8,294.4 / 1,000 = 8.29 h. Battery is 17.7% under 10 kWh.

findings.label: Price per Wh and refill arithmetic (our kit)
findings.value: 8,294.4 Wh; link price $4,369.05 (store $4,599.00); $0.53/Wh; 20.7 h of full sun at rated panel output; pre-order, late January 2027
findings.note: Prices and dispatch are from the brief's "Kits we link" table (store read 2026-11-17). Arithmetic: 4,369.05 / 8,294.4 = $0.527/Wh; 8,294.4 / 400 = 20.74 h, so 400 W of panels refills this battery in about 4 to 5 sunny days at 4.5 sun-hours, before losses.
